## Purpose
`dashboard.ts` and `projects.ts` are the two "surface" modules directly under `src/lib/`: each one owns a cohesive slab of the backend command surface (dashboard-wide reads vs. the project registry/artifact-drift surface) and is the ONLY place that is allowed to call `call()`/`subscribe()` for that surface, per the dashboard guard. They mix DTO interfaces and thin wrapper functions in one file, growing by append as new backend commands land (both files carry a visible history of `// --- <Wave N — spec-slug> ---` section banners marking each addition).

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/lib/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 2
Both files open with a top-of-file comment naming the module's ownership boundary ("Single import site for the dashboard's ... surface. Components MUST NOT reach the transport directly"). `dashboard.ts` re-exports typed unions from `lib/types/*` (`export type { ... } from "@/lib/types/economy"`) rather than redeclaring them locally, and further-appended sections are separated by a one-line `// --- <topic> ---` banner naming the spec/wave that introduced it. `projects.ts` additionally shows the "raw DTO + camelCase mapper" idiom: an internal `RawX` interface mirrors the snake_case wire shape, and an exported `X` interface plus a `toX`/inline `.map()` function converts it once at the wrapper boundary so the rest of the UI never sees snake_case.

## How to apply
A new backend command that belongs to an EXISTING surface (dashboard-wide reads, or the project registry) gets appended to the matching file under a fresh `// --- <topic> ---` banner, with its DTO interface(s) declared immediately above the wrapper function(s) — do not scatter DTOs to a separate types file unless the type is shared with another surface (in that case put it in `lib/types/*` and re-export, as `dashboard.ts` does for economy/specs types). A genuinely new, independent backend surface (its own `call()` family, its own DTOs, not an extension of dashboard/projects) gets its own new `lib/<surface>.ts` file following this same shape, not folded into `dashboard.ts`.
